source.title: The Geometry of Political Abstraction in Large Language Models
source.authors: Noé Durandard; Saurabh Dhawan; Thierry Poibeau

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies distributed residual-stream geometry for political abstraction, not whether individual neurons respond to unrelated inputs. It neither tests nor relies on the polysemanticity claim.
record.gate_note: No neuron-level or MLP-neuron polysemanticity measurements are reported. The rows below capture adjacent findings about cross-domain political representations; they do not test any listed claim version.
record.test_reason: The study probes last-token residual-stream geometry of political stance across policy domains (CCGP, participation ratio). It reports no neuron-level, MLP-neuron or vision-neuron measurements, and no polysemanticity rates. It cites superposition and monosemanticity work only as background, so it neither tests nor relies on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that LLMs transiently compress political stances from different domains into a shared low-dimensional subspace in intermediate layers, which supports cross-domain generalization, with partial re-expansion in later layers. They also note that within-domain decodability is matched by lexical features.
record.recipe_differences: Uses residual-stream extraction, cross-domain linear probing, and participation-ratio geometry; it does not use an individual-neuron analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported abstraction measures vary with layer depth: CCGP peaks and participation ratio reaches minima in intermediate layers, then both trends reverse in later layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-domain political stance probes generalize best in intermediate layers (CCGP above 90% by layer 10) and exceed a TF-IDF baseline, in three 7-8B models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Political stance in LLM residual streams is encoded along a cross-domain shared direction that peaks in middle layers.

fits_no_version.finding: The participation ratio of domain contrast vectors drops from about 7 to 3 or below in middle layers and anti-correlates with CCGP (r about -0.94 to -0.95).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-specific political contrast directions compress into a low-dimensional shared subspace in intermediate layers.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 9th BlackboxNLP Workshop: Analyzing and Interpreting Neural Networks for NLP
record.problems: The authors note that the analysis is correlational, uses synthetic US-centric political statements with binary labels, examines only three mid-sized open-weight models, and pools residual-stream representations at the final token rather than analyzing finer-grained components.

untested.parts: All: no vision models or neurons studied.
All: no MLP-neuron analysis. Authors list MLP sublayers as future work.
All: superposition is cited but not tested.
All: no activation-function, architecture or regularization manipulation of neuron polysemanticity.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation and tranche are correct, and no verdicts are warranted. The WCP result (Section 4, Figure 2) is not a row, but it is irrelevant to all versions.

versions.untested_parts: Individual neurons in vision models and their responses to image inputs.
Polysemanticity of MLP neurons in language models across tokens or contexts.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by representing more features than there are neurons.
Polysemanticity arising from initialization, regularization, or training noise without capacity pressure.
Changes in neuron polysemanticity across activation functions, architectures, or regularization, and associated performance costs.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons have one shared feature or related jobs rather than unrelated mixtures.
Whether neuron polysemanticity judgments depend on activation range or explanation-scoring choices.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct (reported collectively)
rows.stage_stated: Llama-3.1-8B is base; the other two are instruct
rows.operation_detail: Linear SVCs trained within one political policy domain and evaluated on other domains; cross-condition generalization performance (CCGP)

conditions.value: Across network depth; collective trend reported for the three models
Last-token residual-stream representations of political statements

rows.value: Across tested models, CCGP rises from approximately 60% at the input to above 90% by layer 10, peaks in middle layers, and substantially exceeds the lexical baseline there.
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals are shown; numerical intervals not stated
rows.note: The paper reports this common trend across the models, not a combined numerical mean. It measures cross-domain political abstraction, not neuron-level polysemanticity.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. CCGP is a residual-stream probe result on political abstraction, not neuron polysemanticity. It is fine as a fits_no_version finding.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct (reported collectively)
rows.stage_stated: Llama-3.1-8B is base; the other two are instruct
rows.operation_detail: Computed participation ratio from Gram matrices of normalized, domain-specific political contrast vectors

conditions.value: Across network depth; collective trend reported for the three models

rows.measure: Participation ratio (effective dimensionality of political contrast vectors)
rows.value: The participation ratio is approximately 7 in early layers and falls to 3 or below at middle-layer minima; all reported values except the first two layers of OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct are significantly below the permutation null (p ≤ 0.01).
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals are shown; numerical intervals not stated
rows.note: The reported result concerns the geometry of political contrast vectors, not the number or semantic coherence of features encoded by individual neurons.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. Participation ratio of contrast vectors measures alignment of domain directions, not how many features individual neurons encode.

rows.subject: Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, and OLMo-2-1124-7B-Instruct
rows.stage_stated: Llama-3.1-8B is base; the other two are instruct
rows.operation_detail: Correlated layerwise participation ratio with cross-condition generalization performance
rows.measure: Pearson correlation between PR and CCGP
rows.value: Pearson r ≈ −0.94 to −0.95 across all models, p < 0.001
rows.note: This reports co-evolution of two distributed-representation measures, not neuron polysemanticity.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. This is a correlation between two distributed-geometry measures.
